title: 2025 HMMT February Algebra and Number Theory Problem 6
statement: Let \(r\) be the remainder when \(2017^{2025!} - 1\) is divided by 2025!. Compute \(\frac{r}{2025!}\) . (Note that 2017 is prime.)

solutions.text:
Let \(N = 2017^{2025!}\) . Let \(p\) be a prime dividing 2025! other than 2017. Let \(p^{k}\) be the largest power of \(p\) dividing 2025!. Clearly, \(\phi (p^{k}) = (p - 1)p^{k - 1}\) divides 2025! and \(\gcd (2017, p^{k}) = 1\) , so by Euler's Totient Theorem,

\[N\equiv 1\pmod {p^{k}}.\]

Repeating for all such primes \(p\) , we obtain

\[N\equiv 1\pmod {2025! / 2017}.\]

Therefore, \(\frac{2025!}{2017} |N - 1\) , so \(r = \frac{2025!}{2017} s\) for some \(0\leq s< 2017\) . Also, since \(N\equiv 0\) (mod 2017), we have \(r = \frac{2025!}{2017} s\equiv - 1\) (mod 2017).

By Wilson's,

\[\frac{2025!}{2017} = 2016!(2018)(2019)\ldots (2025)\equiv -8!\equiv 20\pmod {2017}.\]

Therefore, \(s\) is negative the inverse of 20 (mod 2017), which is 1311. Our answer is

\[\frac{r}{2025!} = \frac{(2025! / 2017)(1311)}{2025!} = \frac{1311}{2017}.\]
